 Preview: Utah Jazz Kick off NBA Cup Play Against the Dallas Mavericks 
 Eric Spyropoulos ● @EricSpyroNBA Digital Writer November 5, 2026 3:52 PM MST For the Utah Jazz, the start of the 2026-27 has presented significant adversity to fight through.
 Utah’s frontcourt rotation has taken a hit due to injuries to both Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic, while a cold shooting spell has hamstrung the team’s offense. As a result, the Jazz have dropped six games in a row and will look to bounce back to winning ways as they wrap up a four-game road trip.
 Keyonte George (39 points, nine assists) was dynamic Wednesday night against the New Orleans Pelicans, but Utah’s offense struggled down the stretch of overtime in a 120-113 defeat. Lauri Markkanen gutted through some pain and extensive minutes at the five spot as he put up a double-double (21 points, 10 rebounds), but the Jazz went 11-of-47 from deep (23 percent) and couldn’t contain the Pelicans’ downhill attack when it mattered most.
 Next up for the Jazz is a matchup against the Dallas Mavericks on Friday night, which will also serve as Utah’s first NBA Cup Group Stage game. 
 Dallas (4-4) has benefitted from a hot start from Cooper Flagg (24.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 6.3 assists per game) and the return of Kyrie Irving (22.7 points per game), which has resulted in some impressive early victories. The Mavericks won their first Group Stage game a week ago against the Houston Rockets, putting them in prime position to take a clear lead in West Group A following Friday night’s action.
 The two teams split the season series a year ago. 
 Jazz injury report: 
 OUT - Trey Alexander (G League - Two-Way), Harrison Ingram (G League - Two-Way), Jaren Jackson Jr. (Right Knee; MCL Tear), Jusuf Nurkić (Right Foot; 2nd Plantar Plate Tear)
 Mavericks injury report: 
 OUT - Tarik Biberovic (Right Heel; Bursitis), Dereck Lively II (Right Foot; Surgery), Sergio de Larrea (Right Knee; Sprain)
 PROBABLE - Santi Aldama (Right Knee; Surgery), Max Christie (Right Hip; Soreness / Tightness)
 Here are three keys to Friday’s NBA Cup game. 
 Control the possession game  
 Any conversation around a game in today’s NBA will quickly focus on the possession battle.
 With teams looking to maximize their scoring opportunities through offensive rebounding, teams have emphasized crashing and boxing out on the other end of the floor. Ball security is another crucial aspect of the possession game, as teams look to limit their mistakes and force opponents into high-turnover games. 
 Dallas has had success on the offensive glass (12th in offensive rebound percentage), but have struggled mightily on the other end, ranking 29th in opponent offensive rebound percentage. Although Utah hasn’t generated consistent success on the offensive glass to begin this season (18th), Friday’s game could present an opportunity to generate second-chance opportunities. 
 If Utah can limit their turnovers against a Dallas team that hasn’t relied on wrecking havoc on opponent offenses (18th in opponent turnover percentage), the visitors should be able to carve out a key edge in the possession game. 
 Will shots start to fall? 
 A main story of Utah’s recent struggles has been an inability to hit shots. 
 An extended shooting slump has sunk Utah’s offense in recent games, with the Jazz going 34-of-121 from beyond the arc (28 percent) over the last three games. On the season, Utah ranks 27th in 3-point percentage as a squad, having shot just 31.5 percent from deep. 
 “It’s a long year, every team faces adversity and shooting slumps,” Hardy said following the loss to New Orleans. “Ours just happens to be here at the beginning, so it makes it feel a lot worse than maybe it would in two months.” 
 Outside of a lack of ball security, inefficiency has been the main culprit in Utah’s offensive struggles. The Jazz rank 29th in the league in effective field-goal percentage (48.8 percent), highlighting the team’s cold shooting spell. Against a Mavericks defense that ranks 22nd in the league as of Thursday morning, Utah will be looking to snap out of a funk on the offensive end. 
 A battle in the mid-range 
 In the modern NBA, Friday’s matchup between Dallas and Utah will stand out stylistically.
 Both teams rely heavily on mid-range shots to generate offense, eschewing shot attempts at the rim and ranking below the league average in frequency of 3-point attempts.
 Just under 39 percent of Utah’s overall shot attempts have come from the mid-range to begin the season, the highest frequency in the league. Dallas isn’t too far behind, ranking second with 35.9 percent of its shot attempts coming from that area of the floor. Unsurprisingly, the two teams rank 30th and 29th, respectively, in shot attempts coming within four feet of the rim.
 The Mavericks have had more success in the mid-range, ranking third in the league in percentage (49.6 percent). The Jazz have also been efficient from that area of the floor, having connected on 44.2 percent of those looks, good for 10th in the association. 
 Friday’s game tips off at 6 p.m. MT. Tune in to the pregame show with Alema Harrington and Mike Smith beginning at 5:30 p.m. MT on Jazz+!
